evidence.observation: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset."
"Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture."
"Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture."

concerns.recommendation: Turn the comparison into an assertion: name the fixture and a pass/fail bound (for example compact bytes at most N percent of ordinary review bytes, and a maximum absolute byte count for the projected schema), and record in §4 GC1 that the check fails when the bound is exceeded. Otherwise the headline obligation of issue 295 can never be shown to hold or to fail.
concerns.title: Compactness is measured but never bounded, so the core obligation cannot fail

evidence.observation: The version-1 field list is "Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players, direct subtype links and registered constraint signatures." with no scope or partial-view marker.
"The host records actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence."
"explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset" is listed as an issue-295 obligation, but §2 gives it no payload surface.

concerns.recommendation: Add a scope marker plus the set of unresolved includes to the version-1 payload, include both in the digest inputs, and add a GC2 check that a subset render is byte-distinct from the full render of the same model and that the marker names the missing scope. As written, replay from "exact view digest" alone cannot tell a partial context from a full one, which is exactly the condition under which §5's "A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty" must fire.
concerns.title: Partial-scope status lives only in the host record, so a subset view is indistinguishable on replay

evidence.observation: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline." and "Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere."
The check list names "deterministic bytes" but no ordering key or serialization rule.

concerns.recommendation: Specify the canonicalization concretely: object-key order, separator and whitespace policy, whether non-ASCII is escaped or emitted literally and under which normalization form, number formatting, and the total ordering key (for example code-point order on the composed ID) used wherever order is not meaningful. Add a GC1 check that compares emitted bytes across two fresh interpreter processes with varied hash seeds and against a committed golden file, so "deterministic bytes" is falsifiable rather than a same-run self-comparison.
concerns.title: 'Canonical UTF-8 JSON' and 'deterministic ordering' are undefined, so byte parity and digest replay are unfalsifiable

evidence.observation: "Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale."
"Field allowlists and evidence sentinels check disclosure." is stated as a control, not as a phase verification.

"Verify complete identifiers on fixtures, role order, guarded and anchored signatures, deterministic bytes, included elements, empty models, unresolved includes and evidence-only edits." contains no non-disclosure check, and GC2's list does not add one.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit GC1 check that renders a fixture deliberately populated with author evidence, samples, notes and rationale and asserts that no excluded field name, value, or evidence sentinel appears anywhere in the emitted bytes, including inside readings and signatures.
concerns.title: The evidence-exclusion obligation has a control in §6 but no verification in either phase

evidence.observation: "Verify unchanged default output, CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel, direct reuse, a first miss followed by successful lookup of an included fact via its role players, and ambiguous deferral."
Closure runs "repository-prescribed checks, component and layer checks, wheel installation, CLI/API parity, and the packaged host example" but names no pre-change baseline artifact.

concerns.recommendation: Name the compatibility baseline: commit golden bytes for the default (non-opt-in) review rendering captured before the GC2 change, or require the check to diff against the previously released wheel, and state in §4 GC2 that the default path must be byte-identical to that baseline. Without a named baseline, "unchanged default output" cannot be demonstrated to a reviewer.
concerns.title: 'Unchanged default output' names no baseline, so the compatibility claim is unverifiable

evidence.observation: "Use a view digest for replay." with no algorithm or input set, followed by "Check original root bytes and verified transitive include pins before applying evolution because evidence-only changes can preserve the view digest."
"exact view digest" is a required host-record field, so consumers depend on its stability.

concerns.recommendation: State the digest algorithm, whether it covers the canonical payload bytes or a structured field subset, and whether the version marker and unresolved-include set are digest inputs. Add a GC1 check that the same model yields an identical digest across processes, and that an evidence-only edit preserves the digest while a mutated root byte or an unverified transitive include pin is rejected before evolution is applied.
concerns.title: The view digest has no defined algorithm or input set, weakening the replay and stale-state guarantees

evidence.observation: "Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players"
"Loader checks protect composed ID identity." protects the loader, not the renderer's emitted form.
"Verify complete identifiers on fixtures" leaves "complete" undefined, while §5 requires the host to record "inspected IDs".

concerns.recommendation: State in §2 that emitted IDs are exactly the composed loader IDs with no renderer-local aliasing, abbreviation, or re-encoding, and add a GC1 check that every emitted object and fact ID resolves through ModelIndex on the composed model. The compactness pressure noted separately makes ID shortening a likely future temptation, and §5's retry loop depends on those IDs staying resolvable.
concerns.title: Nothing forbids renderer-local ID aliasing, which would break agent-directed lookup by inspected ID

evidence.observation: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline." fixes a version in prose but the enumerated payload contents include no version field.
"Existing additive evolution gates govern writes." implies the underlying model can gain fields after version 1 ships.
"release publication are outside these two phases", so version 1 reaches hosts without a publication gate that could carry the version out-of-band.

concerns.recommendation: Require a version marker inside the payload, define consumer behaviour on an unrecognised version, and state that the projection tolerates model fields added by later additive evolution without changing version 1 semantics. Otherwise digest comparisons across versions are ambiguous and any future field addition is silently breaking for a host that stored only the digest.
concerns.title: The payload carries no version marker, so consumers cannot detect projection version or reject an incompatible one

evidence.observation: "ordered named role players" says nothing about unnamed roles or two roles of the same type on one fact.
"Ordered role-player signatures preserve direction." is the stated control for direction.
"Check the role-specific occurrence before reusing a fact." presumes occurrences are distinguishable per role.

concerns.recommendation: Define the ordering key and the disambiguation rule for anonymous roles, repeated roles of the same type, and multi-role facts, and add a GC1 fixture containing a duplicate-role fact that asserts the emitted signature preserves which player filled which occurrence. Ambiguity here is a direct schema-identity risk because the signature is what an agent reuses a fact on.
concerns.title: Role-player ordering is undefined for anonymous and repeated roles, risking direction and occurrence errors

evidence.observation: "The host owns passage selection, search strategy and prompt budgeting."
"Search indexes, ranking algorithms, hosted inference, new databases, empirical recall claims and release publication are outside these two phases."
"A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty." assumes the agent can tell that its view was cut down.

concerns.recommendation: State in §2 or §3 that the renderer never truncates and always emits a complete projection, that any reduction is a host decision which must flip the partial marker described above, and that the CLI/API surface reports the payload byte size so a host can budget before prompting. Silent truncation by either side is the failure mode that turns a subset miss into a false novelty assertion.
concerns.title: No statement of renderer behaviour when the projection exceeds a host prompt budget

evidence.observation: "The earlier five-phase proposal is archived in historical-fable-draft.md." gives a bare filename with no repository-relative path.
"Record current decisions and exact artifacts."

concerns.recommendation: Give the repository-relative path for historical-fable-draft.md so the archived rationale and the passage-selection experiments cited in §1 are locatable from the plan, matching §8's "exact artifacts" requirement.
concerns.title: The archived prior proposal is cited by bare filename with no path

evidence.observation: "The implementation predates formal review."
"Phase records must link implementation, independent opinions and regression results." requires links but no per-obligation comparison of built behaviour to §2.

concerns.recommendation: Add a closure obligation that each phase record states, for every §2 contract item, whether the as-built renderer matches the plan text, and lists any divergence together with the owner decision that accepted it. Since the code exists already, this is the only place a plan-versus-build drift can be surfaced.
concerns.title: Closure links implementation records but never reconciles as-built behaviour against the §2 contract

summary: The two-phase plan is coherent and correctly keeps search strategy and budgeting with the host, but five product obligations cannot be falsified from the stated evidence: compactness is only measured, never bounded; the canonical byte form and the total ordering rule are undefined; partial-scope status is assigned to the host record rather than the payload, so digest replay cannot distinguish full from subset context; the author-evidence exclusion has a control in section 6 but no named check in section 4; and 'unchanged default output' names no baseline artifact. Five further risks touch schema identity, view-digest definition, payload versioning, role-player ordering for unnamed or duplicate roles, and truncation behaviour. Two completeness items concern an unlocatable archived reference and as-built reconciliation.
